headline: AGNICO EAGLE Q3 BEAT: EPS $2.62, REVENUE +17% ON $4,264 GOLD — Barnat Rock Slide Cuts Output 6%; On Full-Year Guidance
snippet: Agnico Eagle (TSX/NYSE: AEM) posted Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.62 (+21% YoY) on revenue of $3.58B (+17%), driven by a $4,264/oz realized gold price. Gold production fell 6.1% after a July rock mass movement closed the Barnat pit at Canadian Malartic. Cash costs rose 19% to $1,133/oz on higher royalties and fuel. The company is on track for full-year guidance; Barnat pit reopened September 27, ahead of schedule.

headline: KINROSS Q3: EPS $0.50 BEATS YEAR-AGO; FIRST GOLD AT REDBIRD — Capital Returns Raised to 50%, 5% of Shares Bought Back
snippet: Kinross Gold (TSX/NYSE: KGC) reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $0.50 vs $0.44 a year ago. Operating cash flow fell to $714M from $1,024M on higher capex and working capital use. The company poured first gold at the Redbird project and raised its shareholder returns commitment to 50% of free cash flow, having already repurchased 5% of shares outstanding since April 2025.

headline: FIRST MAJESTIC Q3 SILVER FALLS 11% ON SAN DIMAS LABOR DISPUTE — Stock -7% Oct 31; Full Financials Due Nov 5
snippet: First Majestic Silver (NYSE: AG) reported Q3 2026 silver production down 11% year-over-year after a labor dispute disrupted output at its San Dimas mine in Mexico. Shares fell 6.98% on October 31. Full Q3 financial results including costs and earnings are scheduled for November 5, 2026. First Majestic operates mines in Mexico and the United States.

headline: FIREFLY METALS STRIKES SECOND VMS AT GREEN BAY — 22.5m @ 2.5% CuEq at Mount Joy; 2.6km from Nugget Pond Mill
snippet: FireFly Metals (TSX: FFM) discovered a new copper-gold VMS system at Mount Joy Prospect within its Green Bay project in Newfoundland. Lead hole FFR26-071 returned 22.5m @ 2.5% CuEq including 9.0m @ 3.9% CuEq (3.0% Cu, 1.0 g/t Au). The discovery sits 2.6km from the Nugget Pond processing facility and 35km from the flagship Ming Mine. It is the first drilling in the Tilt Cove–Betts Cove district.

headline: CAMECO NARROWS 2026 URANIUM GUIDANCE TO 19.5–20.5Mlb — Key Lake Annual Maintenance Clips Upper Range by 1 Million Pounds
snippet: Cameco (TSX/NYSE: CCO/CCJ) trimmed its 2026 uranium production guidance to 19.5–20.5 million pounds from 19.5–21.5 million pounds, citing Key Lake mill annual maintenance that included new infrastructure installation. McArthur River/Key Lake Q3 output was 1.1Mlb (company share) vs 2.2Mlb in Q3 2025. Nine-month production of 6.9Mlb remains on track within the narrowed range.

headline: WORKER CRITICALLY HURT AT INDIA'S NARWA PAHAR URANIUM MINE — UCIL Union Demands High-Level Government Safety Probe Nov 1
snippet: A worker was critically injured at UCIL's Narwa Pahar underground uranium mine in Jharkhand, India on November 1, 2026. Mine workers' unions have called for a high-level government safety probe. UCIL (Uranium Corporation of India Limited) is a state-owned enterprise operating India's domestic uranium mines for fuel cycle supply.

headline: CHINA'S RARE EARTH INDEX MASKS 16X DYSPROSIUM PRICE GAP — Crucial Disconnect Exposed Ahead of Nov 10 Export-Quota Deadline
snippet: China's official composite rare earth price index understates the true market cost of heavy rare earths like dysprosium by as much as 16x, market analysts say. The divergence has direct implications for Western downstream manufacturers reliant on dysprosium for EV motors and wind turbines. Attention is focused on Beijing's November 10 decision on whether to extend its rare earth export quota suspension.

headline: ENERGY FUELS TARGETS CHINA'S RARE EARTH GRIP — White Mesa Mill Expanding to 10,000 T/Yr Monazite; Full Revenue by 2028–30
snippet: Energy Fuels (NYSE: UUUU), headquartered in Lakewood, Colorado, is expanding rare earth processing at its White Mesa Mill in Utah toward a Phase 1 capacity of 10,000 tonnes per year of monazite concentrate. Uranium sales currently fund the buildout while rare earth operations ramp. Full commercial rare earth revenues are not expected until 2028–2030, with the company's Australian Strategic Materials acquisition adding a mine-to-metal pathway.

headline: LITHIUM STOCKS SINK TO 6-MONTH LOWS — 2027 Surplus Fears and Rate Pressure Rout LatAm Producers; Albemarle Q3 Due Nov 4
snippet: Lithium equities fell to six-month lows on October 30 as analysts flagged a potential 2027 global oversupply and rising U.S. rates squeezed speculative positions. Chilean and Argentine producers including Albemarle, SQM, and Lithium Americas each fell 4–7%. Zimbabwe's Chamber of Mines separately warned that weak global lithium prices are constraining capital despite record export revenues. Albemarle's Q3 results on November 4 will be the sector's next major catalyst.

headline: STONEX: GOLD ENTERS SEASONALLY FAVORABLE NOVEMBER WINDOW — Averages +1% After October's Worst Seasonal Stretch of the Year
snippet: StoneX commodity research notes that gold has historically averaged a 1% gain in November, immediately following October which is statistically the year's weakest seasonal window. The bank's data shows November gold has risen 43.9% of the time after falling in October. With gold down $146 in October to a 2026 year-low near $3,874, some analysts argue the seasonal tailwind sets up a year-end recovery toward the $4,000 level.
